items.excerpt: Heavy rain and strong winds have also caused disruption across British Columbia, Canada, over the last week Storm Charles has brought destructive weather to the Iberian peninsula this week, particularly in Portugal and the far south of Spain. Heavy rain and strong south-westerly winds arrived first in the Portuguese island of Madeira, before the system headed towards the mainland on 11 November. A wind gust of 84.5mph (136 km/h) was recorded at Funchal airport, alongside rainfall totals reaching 355mm (13.97in) in 12 hours. In Lisbon, 183 flights were cancelled on Wednesday, about a third of its normal daily traffic, while Madrid Barajas airport had 155 cancellations. After causing widespread flooding in Spain and Portugal, the system moved on a north-easterly track through southern France and then towards northern Italy. This resulted in significant flooding in parts of Cannes, some of which caused rock falls and led to the closure of roads along the French Riviera. The Italian weather service issued a red rainfall warning, its highest level, for the area extending from Tuscany to Venezia. items.title: ‘Digital arrest’ for 2 months: How fake cops duped 71-year-old retired executive of Rs 6.3 crore
items.excerpt: A 71-year-old retired executive was defrauded of Rs 6.3 crore by alleged fraudsters posing as police officers. After receiving a suspicious video call, she was coerced into signing a non-disclosure agreement and transferring her savings. Over two months, she made eight transactions under the pretense of a money laundering investigation. The Cyber police intervened and managed to recover Rs 2.75 crore after freezing several accounts.
